question.text: Before a fund makes capital calls and commences investing, TVPI is typically:

answer.text: Less than 1 (due to fees and expenses already charged)

explanation.text: The Logic: Before the fund makes capital calls and starts investing, TVPI is less than 1 because the fund corpus is reduced by fees and expenses chargeable to it. The Trap: TVPI of 1 or more requires NAV appreciation that has not yet happened, and exactly zero would imply the fund has no remaining value, which is not the case once it has received commitments. Note: Per workbook page 202.
